notes: SalesDB and InventoryDB consolidated into one database, schema public
Column names converted 1:1 to snake_case; keys keep their names (OrderId → order_id)
INT IDENTITY → GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY; resync sequences with setval after the data load
Filtered unique index on Customers.ExternalId → plain UNIQUE (PostgreSQL allows many NULLs)
DEFAULT SYSDATETIME() → clock_timestamp()::TIMESTAMP; BIT → BOOLEAN; MONEY → NUMERIC(19,4)
Proc ends in a SELECT → FUNCTION RETURNS TABLE(adjustment_id, previous_stock, new_stock)
Previous version was a PROCEDURE with COMMIT/ROLLBACK inside an EXCEPTION block, which PostgreSQL rejects at runtime
WITH (UPDLOCK, ROWLOCK) → SELECT ... FOR UPDATE
TRY/CATCH that only rolls back and re-raises → no EXCEPTION block; the call is atomic
SCOPE_IDENTITY() → RETURNING audit_id INTO
Table variable used only for an @@ROWCOUNT check → RETURN QUERY + IF NOT FOUND (STABLE, no temp table)
ORDER BY ... DESC NULLS LAST to match SQL Server NULL ordering
DATEDIFF(day) → date subtraction; CONVERT(..., 101) → TO_CHAR 'MM/DD/YYYY'
#ReorderQueue → TEMP TABLE IF NOT EXISTS + TRUNCATE
OUTPUT INSERTED.* INTO @CreatedOrders → INSERT ... RETURNING inside a CTE
TOP (@MaxOrders) → LIMIT
SOURCE BEHAVIOUR PRESERVED: @EndDate = EOMONTH(...) is midnight, so BETWEEN excludes orders after 00:00 on the last day of the month. Confirm with the report owner before fixing in both systems
Window functions unchanged; MONEY aggregates cast back to NUMERIC(19,4)
Two result sets → two functions; callers replace @IncludeReferrals = 1 by also calling the _referrals function
Replaces the old get_customer_stats / get_customer_referral_tree names (get_customer_referral_tree collided with customer_orders.sql)
DATEDIFF(month) → month-boundary arithmetic (not AGE())
SOURCE BEHAVIOUR PRESERVED: DATE @EndDate compares as 00:00, excluding the rest of the last day
DATEADD(week, DATEDIFF(week, 0, d), 0) → DATE_TRUNC('week', d + 1 day): Sunday maps to the following Monday, as in SQL Server
sp_executesql → RETURN QUERY EXECUTE format(...) USING

SOURCE BUG PRESERVED: 'SELECT @Discount = ...' leaves @Discount = 0 for an unknown/expired coupon, so the 'invalid coupon' error never fires and the order is accepted at full price. Kept for parity; flagged TODO in code
SELECT ... INTO + IF FOUND reproduces T-SQL no-row assignment semantics
LIKE under a case-insensitive collation → ILIKE
FORMAT 'MMM d, yyyy' → TO_CHAR 'Mon FMDD, YYYY'; CONVERT(EOMONTH, 101) → TO_CHAR
OFFSET/FETCH → LIMIT/OFFSET
Cursor → FOR loop; #RestockQueue → TEMP TABLE
Write-only @RefundedLines table variable dropped
TRY/CATCH that only rolls back and re-raises → no EXCEPTION block
Two result sets → two functions (split naming <base>_<result_set>)
_referrals duplicates get_customer_lifetime_value_referrals logic — consolidation candidate after cut-over
DATEDIFF(year) → year difference (not true age); REPLICATE(n<0) → NULL guard; CONVERT(VARCHAR(10), dt, 120) → date only
MERGE with NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE + OUTPUT $action → PG 17 MERGE ... RETURNING merge_action() inside WITH
BY SOURCE → UPDATE is reported as 'UPDATE' (as SQL Server does), not 'DELETE'
PG 15/16 fallback documented in the function header
RETURNS TABLE instead of SETOF RECORD (column list is fixed)
Sort-column whitelist is case-insensitive like the source and also accepts snake_case names
CHARINDEX('', x) = 0 and case-insensitive matching preserved
NEWID() → gen_random_uuid() (core, no pgcrypto)
FORMAT 'yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss' → TO_CHAR 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS'
INTENTIONAL DIFFERENCE: the source has no BEGIN TRAN, so a failed OrderLines insert left the order committed; the function is atomic
Per-order COMMIT (outside the per-order EXCEPTION block) reproduces the source's autocommit behaviour
Must be CALLed at top level, not inside a transaction block
MERGE ... OUTPUT $action → PG 17 MERGE ... RETURNING merge_action(); ON CONFLICT fallback noted
sp_executesql parameter order kept for $1..$7
LIKE → ILIKE
